container_info.description: This project aims to develop a comprehensive functional test plan for Wi-Fi 7 (IEEE 802.11be) devices, focusing on non-performance aspects. The plan will cover Multi-Link Operation (MLO) with mandatory Multi-Link Single Radio (MLSR) and optional Multi-Link Multi Radio (MLMR) scenarios, security validation for WPA2 and WPA3 protocols, and basic stability test cases. The outcome will be a structured, reusable test plan suitable for device certification, QA, and interoperability testing.
container_info.reasoning: The project is a structured, reusable test plan and supporting tooling for device certification/QA — a server-side backend (APIs, documentation generation, test orchestration) is the natural platform. The container is labeled backend and already includes Python3, pip, Flask, uvicorn and many CLI/dev tools. Flask is a lightweight, minimal Python web/backend framework suitable for headless container operation, simple APIs, documentation endpoints (Sphinx/MkDocs integration), and orchestration tasks. It matches the Minimal Requirements and Lightweight Optimization rules (uses built-in dev server for simple use, minimal dependencies).
requirements: virtualenv or venv for isolated environment (python3 -m venv .venv)
Flask (minimal web framework) installed in venv
uvicorn (present) or Flask built-in dev server for running endpoints
pytest (lightweight testing) for basic unit/integration tests
mkdocs or sphinx (present) for generating documentation; minimal config files
basic configuration files: requirements.txt (Flask, pytest, uvicorn if used), minimal app.py or package with a small API/router
lightweight storage: use file-based storage or SQLite (sqlite3 included in Python stdlib) for any small persistence needs
headless-friendly start script (e.g., python -m flask run or uvicorn app:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000) without production servers
minimal CI/test runner script to invoke pytest and docs build (mkdocs build / sphinx-build) inside the container

steps.name: environment
steps.description: Ensure python venv support is present (install python3-venv if the standard 'venv' module is missing), create an idempotent /etc/profile.d script exporting PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1. Use trap to clean temporary files on failure and validate python3 is available. Operates in workspace: /home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
# Ensure venv available; install system package only if needed
if ! python3 -c 'import venv' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sudo apt-get update -q >/dev/null && sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -qq python3-venv >/dev/null || { echo 'apt install python3-venv failed' >&2; exit 11; }
fi
# Idempotent /etc/profile.d write with tmpfile cleanup
TMPFILE=$(mktemp) || { echo 'mktemp failed' >&2; exit 12; }
trap 'rm -f "${TMPFILE}"' EXIT
cat > "$TMPFILE" <<'EOF'
# CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub: minimal global env
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
EOF
if ! sudo test -f /etc/profile.d/coredoc_govhub.sh || ! sudo cmp -s "$TMPFILE" /etc/profile.d/coredoc_govhub.sh; then
  sudo mv "$TMPFILE" /etc/profile.d/coredoc_govhub.sh && sudo chmod 0644 /etc/profile.d/coredoc_govhub.sh || { echo '/etc/profile.d install failed' >&2; exit 13; }
else
  rm -f "$TMPFILE"
fi
trap - EXIT
# Quick validation (non-login shell): source explicitly to verify file content
bash -lc "source /etc/profile.d/coredoc_govhub.sh && python3 --version >/dev/null" || { echo 'python3 not usable' >&2; exit 14; }

steps.description: Create project layout in the workspace, initialize a python venv idempotently, generate a minimal Flask package (app/__init__.py) with /health and /dbinfo endpoints using an absolute DB path, create a clean requirements.txt (no inline guidance/comments), mkdocs.yml and docs/index.md, generate headless start.sh that uses the venv python explicitly and mirrors validation's safe startup approach, and create ci_run.sh. All file operations use the workspace path.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE" && cd "$WORKSPACE"
# Create venv idempotently
if [ ! -d "$WORKSPACE/.venv" ]; then
  python3 -m venv "$WORKSPACE/.venv"
fi
VENV_PY="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"
# Minimal requirements (explicit packages only)
cat > "$WORKSPACE/requirements.txt" <<'REQ'
Flask>=2.0,<3.0
pytest>=7.0,<8.0
REQ
# App package with absolute sqlite path
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE/app"
cat > "$WORKSPACE/app/__init__.py" <<'PY'
import os
from flask import Flask, jsonify
from sqlite3 import connect

DB_PATH = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', 'data.db'))

def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    @app.route('/health')
    def health():
        return jsonify(status='ok')
    @app.route('/dbinfo')
    def dbinfo():
        conn = connect(DB_PATH)
        cur = conn.cursor()
        cur.execute('CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS kv (k TEXT PRIMARY KEY, v TEXT)')
        conn.commit()
        conn.close()
        return jsonify(db='sqlite', file=DB_PATH)
    return app

app = create_app()
PY
# mkdocs minimal config and docs
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE/docs"
cat > "$WORKSPACE/mkdocs.yml" <<'YML'
site_name: CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub
nav:
  - Home: index.md
YML
cat > "$WORKSPACE/docs/index.md" <<'MD'
# CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub
Minimal documentation scaffold.
MD
# Start script: use venv python explicitly and start in background using safe wrapper
cat > "$WORKSPACE/start.sh" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
VENV_PY="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
export FLASK_APP=app
# Start app in background, write pid and pgid for symmetry with validation
( exec "$VENV_PY" -m flask run --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 > "$WORKSPACE/logs/start.log" 2>&1 ) &
CHILD=$!
# derive numeric PGID
PGID=$(ps -o pgid= "$CHILD" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')
printf "%s\n" "$CHILD" > "$WORKSPACE/.server.pid"
printf "%s\n" "${PGID:-}" > "$WORKSPACE/.server.pgid"
exec wait "$CHILD"
SH
chmod +x "$WORKSPACE/start.sh"
# CI runner script: run tests then build docs
cat > "$WORKSPACE/ci_run.sh" <<'CI'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
VENV_PY="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
# Use venv python for tests; rely on global mkdocs from image
"$VENV_PY" -m pytest -q || { echo 'pytest failed' >&2; exit 2; }
if command -v mkdocs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  mkdocs build -f "$WORKSPACE"/mkdocs.yml -d "$WORKSPACE"/site || { echo 'mkdocs build failed' >&2; exit 3; }
else
  echo 'mkdocs not found in PATH' >&2; exit 4
fi
CI
chmod +x "$WORKSPACE/ci_run.sh"
# gitignore, README, ensure logs dir
cat > "$WORKSPACE/.gitignore" <<G
.venv/
__pycache__/
site/
data.db
G
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE/logs"
echo "CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub - scaffold" > "$WORKSPACE/README.md"

WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
VENV_PY="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"

steps.name: validation
steps.description: Build docs (mkdocs), run tests, start the Flask server with a portable, robust background launcher that writes numeric PID and PGID, wait for readiness with configurable timeout while logging progress and using curl --max-time, probe /health and /dbinfo, capture evidence, then stop the server cleanly by killing the process group with defensive numeric checks and a pkill fallback. Depends on all prior steps.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
VENV_PY="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
# Verify mkdocs exists and print version
if command -v mkdocs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  mkdocs --version || true
else
  echo 'mkdocs not found in PATH' >&2
fi
# Build docs (non-fatal but report)
if command -v mkdocs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  mkdocs build -f "$WORKSPACE"/mkdocs.yml -d "$WORKSPACE"/site >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo 'mkdocs build failed' >&2
fi
# Run tests
"$VENV_PY" -m pytest -q
# Start server robustly: background subshell writes PID; derive numeric PGID
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE/logs"
LOG="$WORKSPACE/logs/server.log"
TIMEOUT=${VALIDATION_TIMEOUT:-30}
# Launch server in background, using explicit venv python; write child pid
( exec "$VENV_PY" -m flask run --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 >"$LOG" 2>&1 ) &
CHILD=$!
# derive PGID numerically
PGID=$(ps -o pgid= "$CHILD" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)
# Validate numeric PID/PGID
if ! [[ "$CHILD" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then echo 'invalid child pid' >&2; exit 20; fi
if [ -z "$PGID" ] || ! [[ "$PGID" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then PGID=''; fi
printf "%s\n" "$CHILD" > "$WORKSPACE/.server.pid"
printf "%s\n" "${PGID}" > "$WORKSPACE/.server.pgid"
# Wait for readiness
SEEN=0
for i in $(seq 1 $TIMEOUT); do
  if curl -sS --max-time 2 --fail http://127.0.0.1:8000/health >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    SEEN=1; break
  fi
  if (( i % 5 == 0 )); then tail -n 20 "$LOG" || true; fi
  sleep 1
done
if [ "$SEEN" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "server failed to become ready within ${TIMEOUT}s, tailing logs:" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2 || true
  # Attempt safe cleanup: use PGID if numeric, else try pkill
  if [[ "$PGID" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    kill -TERM -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  else
    pkill -f "${VENV_PY}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
  rm -f "$WORKSPACE/.server.pid" "$WORKSPACE/.server.pgid"
  exit 21
fi
# Probe endpoints and print evidence
